result.topic_en: Euler explains why the outflow velocity v can exceed the velocity due to the height q when the upper vessel is not much larger than the orifice, why v becomes infinite when the orifice equals the upper vessel's area (continuous acceleration), and concludes that experiments require a very wide upper vessel so that kk can be neglected relative to ff.

items.english: then indeed v > q, i.e. the water would flow out with greater speed than in the preceding case

items.english: in this case (kk = ff) the motion of the water is continually accelerated and never reaches a uniform state
